behavior: Gmail send_email/gmail_send_email and Slack send_channel_message/slack_post_message acquire a durable piece-dispatch fence before provider execution. Reauthorization cannot dispatch again while the result is unknown. A saved completion is returned without another send even if its acknowledgement was lost.

Generic exceptions after direct dispatch remain unknown, not not-started. A secondary audit failure cannot erase a primary completion. Partial results survive crash/restart; RUN_FLOW maxAttempts stays ONE.

Exact native OAUTH2 readback is supported for Gmail 0.17.0 saved message IDs and Slack 0.21.0 bot top-level channel/timestamp receipts without file uploads. The credential must match the literal pinned connection and digest captured at dispatch. Only GET requests to fixed provider hosts are made.

A succeeded top-level run-step output may supply a missing direct receipt for exact provider readback. Confirmation updates the recovery projection, never the original dispatch fence or terminal run. Loop outputs are not guessed.

Unsupported or inconclusive evidence requires inspection and a new intentional run through existing checks. An inspection acknowledges current evidence without claiming that an action succeeded or did not happen. Late completion invalidates the acknowledgement.

Recovery choices are revision-bound and idempotent by request ID, with append-only audit receipts committed atomically. Concurrent or stale decisions cannot overwrite evidence. No recovery choice executes, resumes, enqueues or grants approval.
Run, effects and work-item views share one RecoveryProjection. The recovery inbox paginates terminal incomplete runs needing attention. No Brief UI is activated.
Recovery includes untracked failed/interrupted graph steps, distinguishing loop instances and synthetic queue failure markers. A completed tracked action cannot hide uncertainty in another action.

Confirmed provider evidence is bound to the exact effect/request/version/connection/receipt and survives later inconclusive or blocked lookups and unrelated run progress. Every attempt remains auditable; changed provider receipts cannot borrow confirmation.
Typed Slack completion evidence remains completed for user-mode, threaded and upload-mode receipts even when readback is unsupported; malformed results remain unknown.

migration: Additive workflow_recovery_receipt table, unique (run_id, request_id), retained across run deletion for audit; optional providerBinding on effect records. No destructive DDL or rewriting unknown effects.
rollback: Stop/drain workers, revert Q-07 and rebuild daemon/engine together. Retain audit/effect records. Never resume runs with piece-dispatch records on older binaries, which cannot enforce this fence; inspect them and start new intentional runs if appropriate.
limitations: No general exactly-once external execution; provider SDK internal retries remain outside the Jarvis redispatch guarantee.
Missing provider IDs, permissions, deletions, timeouts, malformed/oversized responses and absent evidence remain inconclusive; no proof of no-send is inferred.
Managed/custom/dynamic credentials, rotated OAuth tokens, unverified connector versions, Slack user-token sends, threads and uploads, and other actions have no Q-07 lookup adapter.
Confirmation proves the exact provider message exists, not delivery/read, remaining-step completion or business success. Inspection never turns unknown into success.

Legacy authorization-only effects may already have executed and require inspection. Mixed old/new engine deployment is not certified. Main plus the full Brief stack requires separate integration verification.
Recovery views and audit history are additive APIs; this card does not ship a dashboard recovery UI.
